title: OpenTideConstants release document
description: DRAFT, format_version 0.6. Schema for OTC_{YYYYMMDD}.json. Each line of OTC_{YYYYMMDD}.jsonl (and of the optional OTC_{YYYYMMDD}.jsonl.gz) is one station document, valid against #/$defs/station. OTC_{YYYYMMDD}.meta.json is the same document without `stations`, valid against #/$defs/meta, so a .jsonl reader can get the conventions, licences, constituent table and release metadata. Units: metres, metres per second (current amplitudes), degrees, degrees per hour, UTC. Every pattern ends with $(?![\s\S]) so that a validator whose $ also matches before a final newline (Python re) still rejects one. Cross-references (convention_id, licence_id, recommended_set_id, constituent names, default_current_bin, current_offsets reference_station_id and reference_bin) must resolve inside the same release, alias ids must be unique within each alias system across the release, and bin numbers must be unique within a set's current_bins and within a station's current_offsets. JSON Schema cannot express these, so the release build checks them separately. The build also checks: (1) a no_constants set with too_short has fewer than release.fit_min_good_hours hours of good data, and every set with constants fitted from a record has at least that many; good_hours is never more than the hours between record_span start and end; (2) a station's recommended set is never a no_constants set, never a short_record set when the station has a set of the same quantity with constants and more good_hours, and always has the quantity of the station's kind; (3) a time_base correction has from different from to, its from equals declared and its to equals published, and an unverified or disputed time_base has published equal to declared; (4) a tombstone's merged_into names an active station whose aliases include every alias id the removed station had; (5) provenance.carried_from_release is earlier than the release datestamp and names a release that held the same set_id, and a carried set's convention_id and licence_id exist in this release; (6) recommended_set_id is null on a reference station only when every set of the station is no_constants (the schema checks this too), and a subordinate station has constant sets, subordinate_offsets or current_offsets (the schema checks this too).

constituents.description: Release-level constituent table: one row per constituent name and constituent_table_version that the release uses.

meta.description: OTC_{YYYYMMDD}.meta.json: the release document without stations.

format_version.description: MAJOR.MINOR. A new optional field is a minor change. A removed or renamed field, or a changed unit or convention, is a major change. A change to an enum (a new value, or a value that is not valid any more) is a minor change for the schema, but it can change what a reader does with a set, so it raises release.min_reader_version. A deprecated field or value is valid for one more minor version.

datestamp.description: Release id: YYYYMMDD in UTC, the day the release was built, with an optional .N counter for a second release on the same day.

min_reader_version.description: Always 0.6 in this schema. The oldest format version a reader must understand to use this release safely, MAJOR.MINOR. A reader that supports only an older version must not use the release, and stays on its last release (the latest pointer per format major and OTC_index.json carry the same value). 0.6 sets it to 0.6: a 0.5 reader filters out only qc_status excluded, so it would treat a no_constants set as usable. Readers before 0.6 do not read this field; for them the publish gate holds: no 0.6 release is published until the SDK releases that read 0.6 are out.

fit_min_good_hours.description: The minimum hours of good data this build needs to fit constants (about 15 days, 360 hours). A record with fewer is a no_constants set with no_constants_reason too_short.

doi.description: Deprecated in 0.6, and always null. A Zenodo version DOI is minted after the release files are fixed, and not every release gets one, so a release file never carries it. The version DOI, when a release has one, is only in OTC_index.json and the latest pointers, as zenodo_version_doi. Writers may leave this field out.

concept_doi.description: The concept DOI: the one DOI for all Zenodo versions of OpenTideConstants. Cite a release by this DOI and the release datestamp. Null only before the concept DOI exists.

phase_reference.description: Phase reference of the source data before conversion. Published phases are always Greenwich (UTC).

v0_model.description: Astronomical-argument model, e.g. schureman_tcd or tamura_iho2006.

nodal_formula_ids.description: Node-factor formula id per constituent name, when nodal_handling is f_u_at_prediction.

canary.description: Result of the per-source convention check that confirmed this convention.

spdx.description: SPDX id, or a LicenseRef- id where SPDX has none (e.g. LicenseRef-PublicDomain-USGov).

constituent_name.description: OTC canonical constituent name. At most 15 characters, so that a C reader can hold it in char[16].

nodal_formula_id.description: Node-factor formula id, as in convention.nodal_formula_ids.

station_id.description: Stable id in the OTC namespace. Never changed, never reused.

tombstone.description: A station id that is not used any more, because the station was merged into another station or was a duplicate of one. The row keeps the id from being reused and points to the station that holds its records. These are the only reasons: a station is never removed because its records are short, broken or from a source that failed a check. Those records stay as constant sets with their annotations. The release build checks that merged_into is an active station whose aliases include every alias id of the removed station.

removed_reason.description: merged: the station and another one are the same gauge, and its records now belong to merged_into. duplicate: the station repeated merged_into.

merged_into.description: The OTC station id that holds this station's records.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name of the station, e.g. Europe/Oslo, for showing local times. Constants and phases stay in UTC.

aliases.description: Ids of the same station in other systems. Within one release an alias id is unique within its system: no two stations share a noaa id, a gesla id, and so on. The release build checks this.

linz.description: LINZ site id: the prefix of its *_Harm_* file name, e.g. 077NELSON.

shom.description: SHOM REFMAR tide gauge id (shom_id), e.g. 3 for Brest.

pegelonline.description: PEGELONLINE station uuid, e.g. aad49293-242a-43ad-a8b1-e91d7792c4b2 for Cuxhaven Steubenhöft. Not the shortname, which can change.

rws.description: Rijkswaterstaat Waterwebservices location code, e.g. hoekvanholland.

mi.description: Marine Institute Irish National Tide Gauge Network station_id, e.g. Ballycotton Harbour.

dmi.description: DMI oceanObs stationId, e.g. 20002 for Skagen Havn.

smhi.description: SMHI oceanographic observation station id, e.g. 2545 for Arkö.

uhslc.description: UHSLC station number, three digits as in the Fast Delivery file name h{NNN}.csv, e.g. 001.

recommended_set_id.description: The set_id of the set chosen by the published recommendation rule, or null for a subordinate station with offsets only, or for a station whose every set is no_constants. Only sets of one quantity compete: water-level sets for a tide station, current sets for a current station. The recommended set is never a no_constants set. A set flagged short_record never outranks a set of the same quantity at the same station that has constants and more hours of good data (record_span.good_hours). The release build checks these.

default_current_bin.description: Current stations only: the bin to show by default (NOAA currbin). It names a bin of the recommended set's current_bins, or of current_offsets for a subordinate current station.

current_offsets.description: Subordinate current stations only: one entry per bin, each tied to a bin of a reference current station, as NOAA currentpredictionoffsets gives them.

source_type.description: official: constants published by the agency that runs the gauge; gauge: an OTC fit to gauge observations; model: interpolated from a global tide model.

quantity.description: What the constants predict. A station's kind comes from its recommended set, or from its reference station's recommended set if it is subordinate.

good_hours.description: Hours of good data in the record, after quality control. Required on every set fitted from a gauge record. This is the record length that decides which constituents can be fitted, whether constants are fitted at all, and how a set ranks. start and end give the span.

named.description: Named datums in metres relative to the constants' zero, as the source gives them.

qc_status.description: ok: constants are published and qc_flags is empty. flagged: constants are published and qc_flags says what to know about them. no_constants: the set is listed but no constants were fitted; no_constants_reason says why, and qc_flags has at least one flag. No status marks a record as removed: every record stays listed. excluded is not valid in 0.6. accepted and fallback are deprecated: read accepted as ok, or as flagged when qc_flags has a flag; read fallback as a set carried over from an earlier release (provenance.carried_from_release). A writer uses ok, flagged or no_constants.

record_issues.description: What is wrong with a broken record. The set stays listed. When a usable segment exists, fit_segment names it and the constants are fitted to it; when none exists, qc_status is no_constants.

fit_segment.description: The part of a broken record that the constants are fitted to. Absent when the whole record is fitted.

no_constants_reason.description: Only with qc_status no_constants. too_short: less than about 15 days of good data (needs the short_record flag). fit_unusable: the record is broken and no segment gives a usable fit; record_issues says what is wrong.

constituents.description: Water-level constituents. Empty for a current set, whose constants are in current_bins, and for a no_constants set.

current_bins.description: Current sets only: tidal-current ellipse constants, one entry per depth bin.

dropped_constituents.description: Constituents left out of this set, each with its reason. For a short record these are the constituents the record is too short to separate (rayleigh).

not_separable_from.description: With dropped_reason rayleigh: the kept constituent that the record is too short to separate this one from, e.g. K1 for P1.

allOf.description: A current set has current_bins (unless no_constants) and no water-level constituents; a water-level set has no current_bins.
Every set fitted from a gauge record carries a time-base annotation and its hours of good data.
flagged: constants and at least one flag.
A water-level set with qc_status ok or flagged (or the deprecated accepted or fallback) has constants.
no_constants: no constants, a reason, at least one flag, and no expected accuracy. Every other status has no no_constants_reason.
fit_unusable needs record_issues to say what is wrong.
too_short is a short record: it has the short_record flag, which brings in good_hours.
record_issues and the broken_record flag go together.
A short record states its length, and its expected accuracy unless no constants were fitted.
An unverified or disputed time base is flagged, so the set is never ok.
A time_base flag means the set's time base is unverified or disputed.
A carried-over set has the carried_over flag, and the flag has the release it came from. A gate fallback is a carry-over.
The deprecated qc_status fallback is a carried-over set.
The 0.6 time_base replaces provenance.time_base: a set has one or the other.

time_base_label.description: A time-base class: utc_instant; utc_mean_start60 (hourly means stamped at the start of the hour); utc_plus_N or utc_minus_N (UTC plus or minus N whole hours); local_dst:<IANA zone> (local time with daylight saving); step:<date>[,<date>...] (the time base changes at each date).

time_base_annotation.description: The time-base annotation of the record behind a set. verified: the evidence confirms the declared time base. corrected: the evidence shows another class, and the constants are fitted after the correction; this needs positive evidence. unverified: no comparator gives a verdict, so the declared time base (GESLA's, for a GESLA record) is kept. disputed: the evidence disagrees with the declared time base but no class explains it, so the declared time base is kept. Replaces 0.5's free-text provenance.time_base.

reason.description: One line for people, e.g. 'declared utc_instant corrected to utc_mean_start60 by official predictions (kartverket:EXF)'.

declared.description: The time base the source declares for the record.

published.description: The time base the constants were fitted with: declared, unless code is corrected.

correction.description: Only with code corrected: the correction applied, from the declared time base to the published one.

months_dropped.description: Isolated bad months left out of the fit (YYYY-MM). A field of the annotation, not a time-base class: it goes with any code.

decided_in.description: Datestamp of the build that decided this annotation. A later build reuses the decision while the evidence is unchanged.

decided_build_commit.description: The build commit of the build that decided the annotation (decided_in).

allOf.description: verified and disputed rest on evidence; unverified may list what was tried.

time_base_evidence.description: One comparison behind a time-base annotation. comparator_kind: official_predictions (an agency's predictions near the gauge), official_constants (e.g. NOAA harmonic constants for a NOAA record), sibling_record (another record at the same gauge from a different contributor, after its own correction), provider (the verdict of other records from the same provider), model (a global tide model, e.g. EOT20), served_constants (constants already served for the location), dst_selftest (the record's own daylight-saving test).

comparator_id.description: e.g. kartverket:EXA, a GESLA file id, eot20. For dst_selftest, the record's own id.

distance_km.description: Distance from the gauge to the comparator, or null where it has none (a self-test).

lag_min.description: The measured lag or offset in minutes: the record's time stamp of an event minus the comparator's time of the same event. Negative when the record's stamps are early. An hourly mean stamped at the start of its hour is about -30, and its correction moves the stamps by +30 min.

detail.description: Free text for people: what was measured or why a check gave no number.

record_issue.description: One thing wrong with a record. start and end give where it is (a step has only start).

values.description: The numbers behind the issue, e.g. {"step_m": -0.31}.

expected_accuracy.description: How accurate a short record's constants are expected to be, measured by cutting long records down to the same length (cut_to_days) and comparing their fits with the full-length fits. Give the amplitude and phase uncertainty, or the expected prediction error, or both.

calibration_records.description: How many long records were cut down.

amp_uncertainty_m.description: Expected amplitude error of the main constituents (median over the calibration records).

phase_uncertainty_deg.description: Expected phase error of the main constituents.

time_mae_min.description: Expected mean absolute error of high- and low-water times.

height_mae_m.description: Expected mean absolute error of high- and low-water heights.

source_name.description: The source's own name. At most 31 characters, so that a C reader can hold it in char[32].

current_depth_type.description: How depth_m is measured: below_surface (NOAA depthType S), below_chart_datum (NOAA depthType B, which NOAA's metadata API documents as 'below chart datum') or unknown (NOAA depthType U). above_bottom is kept only so that 0.4 data stays valid; no source uses it, and NOAA's B is below_chart_datum, not above_bottom.

current_bin.description: Ellipse constants for one depth bin: per constituent, the amplitude and phase of the current along the major axis (azimuth_deg) and along the minor axis, perpendicular to it, as NOAA harcon gives them.

depth_m.description: Bin depth in metres, or null if the source gives none.

mean_major_ms.description: Mean current along the major axis in metres per second, signed: positive toward azimuth_deg. A constant added to the major-axis harmonic sum at every time. NOAA majorMeanSpeed (cm/s) divided by 100. Absent if the source gives none; a reader then adds 0.

mean_minor_ms.description: Mean current along the minor axis in metres per second, signed in the same sense as the minor-axis harmonic terms. A constant added to the minor-axis harmonic sum at every time. NOAA minorMeanSpeed (cm/s) divided by 100. Absent if the source gives none; a reader then adds 0.

current_constituent.description: One constituent of a current bin. Amplitudes in metres per second (NOAA cm/s divided by 100). Phases are Greenwich phase lags under the set's convention (NOAA majorPhaseGMT and minorPhaseGMT). The mean current is not a constituent: it goes in the bin's mean_major_ms and mean_minor_ms, so the name Z0 is not allowed here.

source_name.description: The source's own name. At most 31 characters, so that a C reader can hold it in char[32].

speed_deg_per_hour.description: Constituent speed, as in the constituent table.

current_offset.description: Offsets for one bin of a subordinate current station. Time adjustments in minutes, added to the reference bin's event times; amplitude ratios multiply the reference bin's speeds. A value the source gives as null stays null.

bin.description: Bin number of this station (the _N suffix of the NOAA id).

qc_flag.description: Something a user of the set needs to know. time_base: the time base is unverified or disputed (see the set's time_base). broken_record: see record_issues. short_record: the record is too short to resolve every candidate constituent; see record_span.good_hours, dropped_constituents and expected_accuracy. carried_over: the source failed a check in this build, so the set keeps its constants from provenance.carried_from_release.

reason.description: One line for people, not blank.

verdict.description: Deprecated in 0.6: free text. Use reason, and the set's time_base for a time_base flag.

provenance.description: Where the set came from and what was done to it. A closed list of keys: qc_status is the only status of a set, so no provenance key can carry one. A new source-specific key is added here first.

analysis_years.description: JMA: the years the agency's analysis used, per period, as the source gives them.

list_distance_km.description: LINZ: distance from the file's header position to the LINZ port list position.

source_constituents_not_published.description: JMA: source constituents that have no OTC name, so they are not in the set.

carried_from_release.description: The datestamp of the earlier release whose constants this set keeps, because its source failed a check in this build. Goes with the carried_over flag.

time_base.description: Deprecated in 0.6: the free-text verdict and correction of 0.5. 0.6 replaces it with the set's time_base, and a set does not have both.

decision.description: How the release gate decided the set. outcome fallback means the set is carried over (carried_from_release).

height_adjusted_type.description: R = ratio, A = additive (metres), as NOAA gives it.

previous_release.description: The same metrics for the previous release, or null.
